senses.gloss: , f. (trutina, τρυτάνη, prob. of Semit. origin, cmp. טְרָא) balance, steel-yard. Sifra K’dosh. Par. 3, ch. VIII במשקל זו טרי׳ ‘in weight’ (Lev. XIX, 35) that means the trutina.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 81a:5">Sabb. 81ᵃ</cite> <he>וכי ט׳ יכניס</he> shall a (gold) balance be brought in (to weigh accurately)?; <cite ref="Menachot 87b:14">Men. 87ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 89a:15">B. Bath. 89ᵃ</cite> <he>ט׳</he> (for weighing gold), contrad. to <cite ref="M00019"><he>מאזנים</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 2:5">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. II, 5</cite>.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 6:4:4">Y. Shek. VI, end, 50ᵇ</cite> <he>כמין ט׳</he> arranged like a steel-yard.

<cite ref="Sotah 34a:10">Sot. 34ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="M00460"><he>מוֹט</he></cite>, <cite ref="Numbers 13:23">Num. XIII, 23</cite>) <he>ט׳ וט׳ דט׳</he> a combination of balancing poles (for four couples of carriers); Y. ib. VII, 21ᵈ bot. <he>טוּרְטיּרִין</he> several poles (each carried by two); <he>ט׳ וטוּרְטוּרֵי טרוטורין</he> a combination &c.—Pl. <cite ref="I00229"><he>טוּרְטָנִין</he></cite>. B. Kam. l. c. Ms. R. 2 (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 400).
